Transcriptional nodes governing diversity and effector rewiring of a plastic liver invariant natural killer T cell ecosystem
Rigidity-driven molecular assembly for high-efficiency flexible perovskite/CIGS tandems
Molecular basis for thermoresponsive protein condensation in plants
Crystal structures of tetraketide synthase reveal the mechanistic basis for partitioning products in cannabinoid biosynthesis
articles.abstract: Abstract Tetraketide synthase (TKS), a plant type III polyketide synthase, catalyzes the iterative condensation of hexanoyl-CoA and three malonyl-CoAs to generate a linear tetraketide-CoA that is cyclized to olivetolic acid (OA), an essential intermediate in cannabinoid biosynthesis. TKS also produces abundant tri- and tetraketide lactones that divert flux from OA. Here, we report crystal structures of TKS in complex with mono-, di-, tri-, and tetraketide intermediates that reflect relevant catalytic states in substrate loading, chain elongation, and cyclization. Met187 acts as a dynamic steric gate governing substrate tolerance and elongation, while adjacent residues maintain intermediates in an extended, linear conformation. Ser332-mediated interactions promote lactonization through C5-O-C1 ring closure, implicating lactonization as an enzyme-controlled process. Recapture-versus-release of the tetraketide intermediate determines whether linear or cyclized products are formed. These findings establish a framework for engineering TKS variants with improved OA production and advance chemoenzymatic methods for producing cannabinoids and structurally diverse polyketides.

articles.title: Evolution tunes functional sub-state interconversion to boost enzyme function
articles.abstract: Abstract Enzymes do not operate as static structures, but continuously sample an ensemble of conformational sub-states with distinct catalytic activities. Yet whether evolution can exploit the transitions between sub-states to improve activity remains largely unexplored. Here, we dissect an evolutionary trajectory of β-lactamase OXA-48 toward enhanced ceftazidime hydrolysis. OXA-48 is well suited for studying sub-state evolution, as equilibria between sub-states can be directly interrogated through substrate-induced inactivation and binding kinetics. Steady-state and pre-steady-state kinetic analyses reveal that evolution perturbed the conformational equilibrium and gradually shifted the rate-limiting step from substrate binding through sub-state interconversion to the chemical step. Kinetics with the native substrate meropenem, confirmed coexisting sub-states with markedly different reactivity to ceftazidime, demonstrating that remodeling the conformational landscape introduced a catalytic trade-off rooted in an incompatibility between the native and evolved sub-state populations. Hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry independently corroborated these coexisting sub-states, while molecular dynamics simulations traced the activity trade-off to increased active-site flexibility around the catalytic base. Together, our findings establish sub-state interconversion as a direct target of evolutionary selection, shaping functional divergence and offering distinct strategies for enzyme engineering and drug design.

articles.title: The human hypothalamus encodes prediction errors during sensory–nutrient inference
articles.abstract: Abstract Humans infer the nutrient content of foods from sensory cues, yet the neural and computational basis of these inferences remains unclear. Here we show how oral texture contributes to judgements of fat content by combining purpose-designed foods that dissociated fat from texture with behavioural testing, computational modelling, functional neuroimaging during consumption, and a naturalistic feeding assay. Judgements of fat content reflected established relationships between oral texture and fat and became systematically less accurate when these relationships were violated. A computational model formalized these failures as prediction errors—discrepancies between fat content predicted from texture and actual fat content. During food consumption, the hypothalamus encoded these model-derived prediction errors, responding most strongly when texture predicted more fat than the food contained. Individual differences in hypothalamic sensitivity to texture predicted fat intake during an ad libitum meal. These findings show how sensory inference of fat content engages hypothalamic signals predicting food intake.

articles.title: Control of out-of-plane anti-damping spin torque with a canted ferromagnetic spin source
Anyone can be the best depending on how structural variant callers are evaluated
articles.abstract: Abstract Structural variants (SVs) are medium- and large-scale genomic alterations that shape phenotypic diversity and disease risk. Numerous methods have been proposed for discovering SVs, however their benchmarking has been inconsistent across studies, often resulting in contradictory findings. We evaluate the performance of several SV discovery methods for detecting unbalanced SVs from long-read sequencing data and observe substantial variation in performance and ranking depending on the choice of ground truth, reference genome, and genomic regions used for evaluation. Our results indicate that these discrepancies largely arise from inconsistencies among SV callsets used as ground truth, ranging from consortium-curated benchmarks to callsets derived from high-quality assemblies. These discrepancies call for additional caution in downstream analyses and in drawing conclusions based on predicted SVs. Our findings underscore the complexity of evaluating SV detection methods and highlight the need for careful consideration and field-standard practices when reporting performance metrics.

articles.title: Changing mercury exposure in the Yukon Watershed linked to traditional diet shifts and permafrost thaw
articles.abstract: Abstract Rapid Arctic warming is disrupting ecosystems and traditional subsistence resources, and simultaneously may release toxic mercury into aquatic ecosystems. Together, these changes threaten food security and public health. In the Yukon River Basin of Alaska, many Indigenous communities that traditionally rely on subsistence fishing are facing precipitous declines in salmon populations. Alternative protein sources can contain up to eight times more mercury, with burbot, northern pike, and beluga being major dietary mercury contributors. More reliance on these proteins could increase mercury exposure, while permafrost thaw is projected to increase mercury concentrations in fish by 21–175% by 2100. Here, we combine diet surveys and subsistence harvest data to develop a hypothetical dietary mercury model. Dietary shifts and permafrost-driven increases in fish mercury could increase mercury intake up to 486%, potentially exceeding public health guidelines and highlighting the vulnerability of Arctic food systems to interacting environmental and ecological change.

articles.title: Dual-comb photoacoustic Brillouin spectroscopy of optomechanical dynamics in gas-filled microstructured hollow-core fibers
Expanding antimicrobial chemical space by engineering drug safety
articles.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) infections are a major health threat. Although advances in high-throughput screening, genome mining, and machine learning have accelerated antimicrobial discovery, insufficient separation between antibacterial efficacy and host toxicity remains a bottleneck to the clinical development of new antimicrobial compounds. Here, we establish a generalizable, two-component strategy to engineer drug safety and mobilize otherwise inaccessible chemical space for antimicrobial therapy, using calicheamicin, a potent cytotoxin with unacceptable host toxicity, as a proof of concept. First, we engineer a conditionally active drug conjugate that limits calicheamicin activity to infected tissue, thereby reducing systemic toxicity. Second, we engineer a self-resistance enzyme from Micromonospora echinospora , the natural producer of calicheamicin, as a long-circulating antidote to neutralize calicheamicin outside infected tissue, further reducing off-target toxicity. The conjugate exhibits activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens upon exposure to a protease present within the infected microenvironment. When delivered with the antidote, antibacterial efficacy is maintained while off-target toxicity is reduced in mouse models of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial pneumonia. We anticipate that our dual strategy, which engineers drug safety rather than selecting for it, provides a generalizable framework for mobilizing promising but toxic compounds as antimicrobials.

articles.title: An all-in-one wearable platform offers continuous assessment and early diagnosis of acute kidney injury for outdoor workers
A membrane-active cationic supramolecule to treat both fungal and bacterial keratitis
Identification and functional characterization of bacterial bilirubin vinyl reductase across vertebrate gut microbiomes
articles.abstract: Abstract Gut bacteria reduce bilirubin to urobilinogen, allowing it to be excreted through feces and urine, but studies have long noted a heterogeneous mixture of partially reduced bilirubin-derived intermediates, suggesting that multiple enzymes are involved. Here we identify bilirubin vinyl reductase (BilV), an Old Yellow Enzyme family reductase encoded in the genomic neighborhood of the known bilirubin reductase ( bilR ). Using heterologous expression and LC–MS/MS, we show that BilR acts on the methine bridges in the bilirubin reduction pathway; co-expression with BilV enables vinyl-group reduction and complete conversion to urobilinogen. In bacterial genomes, bilV co-occurs primarily with the bilR -insertion subtype and is largely absent alongside bilR -short. Analysis of 1,197 gut metagenomes across 14 vertebrate species reveals that this differential co-occurrence shapes pathway availability across hosts: carnivores and omnivores carry balanced bilR and bilV , whereas avian microbiomes, dominated by bilR -short, are depleted for bilV . These findings establish that bilirubin reduction to urobilinogen involves two enzymes with complementary regioselectivity, revising the previous model, and that their distribution across vertebrate gut microbiomes varies in relation to host bile pigment chemistry.

articles.title: Buried stochastic interfaces enabling depth-multiplexed optical physical unclonable functions
Complement as an evolutionary driver of vector-microbe immune evasion enabling pathogen transmission
Interstitial fluid regime transition shapes ovarian follicle morphogenesis
Room-temperature continuous-wave mid-infrared microdisk laser on InP enabled by InAs quantum dots
articles.abstract: Abstract Mid-infrared photonics is important for gas monitoring, non-invasive medical diagnostics, and free-space optical links. Realizing high-density photonic integrated circuits in the short-wave mid-infrared (SW-MIR, 2–3 μm) requires compact, efficient microscale lasers that can be integrated on standard platforms. Conventional quantum-well microcavity lasers cannot sustain efficient operation as cavities shrink because lateral carrier diffusion and surface recombination impose a fundamental limit on the threshold, while Auger recombination and thermal carrier leakage losses severely compromise thermal stability in the SW-MIR window. Here, we demonstrate that the strong carrier localization in self-assembled InAs quantum-dot (QD) gain medium circumvents these limitations. A five-stack InAs/InP QD active region achieves room-temperature continuous-wave single-mode lasing in a suspended 5.5 µm microdisk at 2.064 µm. The device also sustains lasing up to 110 °C under pulsed excitation. Temperature-dependent spectra and electronic structure analysis reveal ground-to-excited state dynamics and suppression of thermal carrier leakage. These results demonstrate the potential of QD gain media for compact SW-MIR light sources on InP and Si photonic platforms.

articles.title:
Field-Scale Dynamics
of Pathogen Indicators, Toxic
Cyanobacteria, and Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Wastewater Reservoir-Irrigated
Produce
articles.abstract: Abstract Treated wastewater (TWW) irrigation is essential for agriculture in arid and semiarid regions. However, it may introduce microbial contaminants, including antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants, to crops, resulting in food safety risks. This study holistically assessed the transfer of pathogens and AMRs from TWW to irrigated crops under field conditions. Five reservoir-stored water sources of varying quality and eight corresponding crops were explored. Samples were analyzed directly and following copiotrophic enrichment to underscore viable pathogen indicators. Cultivation of total and cefotaxime-resistant coliforms and E. coli was used to evaluate pathogen and AMR levels. Concomitantly, pathogen indicators, bacteriophages, and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) were analyzed in selected low- and high-quality water sources and associated crops by using shotgun metagenomics. Coliforms were detected in nearly all samples, whereas cefotaxime-resistant coliforms were confined to lower-quality water. Enrichment-based metagenomics improved the detection of low-abundance, clinically relevant targets, highlighting its value for surveillance. Microbial contamination in water decreased with increasing treatment, but this trend was not reflected in the crops. Elevated Microcystis loads and microcystin-encoding genes in one water profile highlighted the potential risks of effluent storage reservoirs. Although water quality moderately influenced crop resistomes, minimal associations were observed among waterborne pathogens, ARGs, and produce, suggesting additional sources of contamination.

articles.title:
Enabling
Machine-Based Relationship Discovery between
Exposures, Biomarkers, and Clinical Outcomes
articles.abstract: Abstract Causal assessments in environmental health as exemplified by the U.S. EPA’s Integrated Science Assessments (ISAs) require reconciling toxicological and epidemiological evidence expressed in incompatible vocabularies and in quantitative terms. Ontologies, knowledge graphs, collaborative wikis, and large language models each address part of this problem, but there is a need for support for machine-based reasoning over exposure–biomarker–outcome relationships together with uncertainty. Working from the chapter of the PM2.5 ISA covering respiratory associations, a group spanning toxicology, exposure science, epidemiology, and biomedical informatics mapped each element of an exposure-to-outcome conceptual model onto existing semantic resources. There is sufficient coverage across exposures, molecular initiating events, phenotypes, and diseases and their relevant biomarkers; however, what is missing is the capacity to attach effect estimates, uncertainty intervals, study design, at-risk population, and provenance to the relationships among them. A path forward is an ontology-grounded probabilistic knowledge graph, populated by supervised machine-assisted extraction and curated by the domain community. We propose testable pilots, each with explicit validation against the PM2.5 ISA and each executable within a single assessment cycle.

articles.title:
Leveraging
City-Level Transmission Hubs of Water Scarcity
Risk to Reduce Potential Economic Losses
articles.abstract: Abstract Water scarcity not only causes potential local economic losses but also poses risks to supply chains, known as the virtual water scarcity risk (VWSR). While previous research has identified major sources and sinks of VWSRs, the transmission hubs that mediate this risk remain underexplored. This study uncovers sector-wise VWSR transmission hubs at the city level in China from 2012 to 2017 using a structural-path-based betweenness approach. The results show that VWSR transmission hubs are predominantly located in East China, particularly in Suzhou, Hefei, and Nanjing. The sectors of food and tobacco processing, chemical products, textiles, and agriculture are identified as dominant transmission hubs. Improving the production efficiency of these hubs effectively weakens the VWSR transmission, reducing associated potential supply chain economic losses by 18%. Combined interventions targeting transmission hubs, risk sources, and sinks reduce potential supply chain economic losses by 30%. At the regional level, hub-targeted interventions achieve widespread VWSR reductions, whereas sink-targeted supply chain reallocation produces a limited national reduction and even increases VWSR in some regions. This study proposes a city-targetable policy lever of transmission hubs for reducing resource scarcity risks and enhancing supply chain resilience.

articles.title:
Integrated Eco-Efficiency
of Residential Cooling in
Dengue-Prone Climates
articles.abstract: Abstract Rising use of room air conditioners (RACs) in dengue-endemic tropical Asia changes both household energy demand and indoor conditions relevant to dengue transmission, creating a trade-off that appliance-centered life-cycle assessment does not capture. We developed an integrated annual eco-efficiency (IAEE) metric that combines annualized private costs, life-cycle environmental externalities, vector-control costs, and modeled dengue-hospitalization costs at the household scale. A mechanistic transmission model estimated the dengue indoor basic reproduction number across eight cities; machine-learning analysis of observed dengue records provided an independent epidemiological check on the modeled temperature response. In the modeled scenarios, raising RAC set points above approximately 24 °C reduced cooling-related impacts but increased estimated dengue burden in a city-specific manner, whereas lower set points reduced modeled transmission at greater energy and environmental cost. At 24 °C, decentralized-solar RAC scenarios reduced annual environmental costs by 74–91% relative to national-grid RAC scenarios, although private-cost advantages over naturally ventilated configurations occurred only in selected cities. The results identify a city-dependent transition region near 24 °C rather than a universal optimum, with magnitudes subject to the reported 2.5th–97.5th percentile uncertainty intervals.

articles.title: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
Dynamic B–OH intermediates enable photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into formic acid

Decoupling
Physical Effects in the Interfacial Polymerization
of Polyamide Membranes
articles.abstract: Abstract Interfacial polymerization (IP) is widely used to fabricate thin films, including polyamide (PA) for reverse osmosis (RO) desalination membranes. In this process, m-phenylenediamine (MPD) diffuses across a liquid–liquid interface into the organic phase and reacts exothermically with trimesoyl chloride (TMC) to form a thin film. Because common additives simultaneously affect monomer transport and interfacial tension (IFT), isolating the physical parameters governing interfacial instability, film morphology, and membrane formation remains challenging. Here, we decouple these parameters by comparing two common additives, sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and ethyl acetate (EA), at concentrations that yield identical IFT, thereby creating comparable initial susceptibility to instability but distinct MPD transport rates. UV–vis measurements show that EA-modulated IP significantly enhances MPD transport, while particle tracking via confocal microscopy reveals stronger interfacial instabilities. Accordingly, EA-modulated IP produces more crumpled surfaces than SDS-modulated IP, consistent with an established instability-morphology phase diagram, demonstrating that polymerization rate alone can drive the system from stable to unstable regimes. These morphological changes translate into membrane performance, with EA-modified membranes exhibiting higher water permeance without compromising salt rejection. Overall, this work establishes a systematic framework for decoupling physical attributes governing IP and a strategy for rationally leveraging additives to control film morphology and membrane performance.

articles.title:
Apparent
Distribution of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl
Substances between Serum and Cerebrospinal Fluid: Influencing Factors
and Potential Neurotoxic Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract The apparent serum-to-CSF distribution of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) across the blood–cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) and the factors governing this process remain poorly understood in humans, particularly in relation to their potential neurotoxic mechanisms. This study quantified 52 PFAS in 173 paired human serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples. Apparent serum-to-CSF distribution ratios (RCSF/serum) ranged from 0.081 to 1.173. Perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) exhibited a relatively high RCSF/serum, while perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids showed an approximately U-shaped distribution pattern with increasing carbon chain length, suggesting short-chain PFAS warrant as much attention as long-chain PFAS. The group-specific correlation analyses suggested that molecular weight, lipophilicity, HSA binding, and interactions with transporters were potentially important factors shaping the apparent serum-to-CSF distribution of PFAS. Furthermore, network toxicology prioritized the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling pathway, and in vitro experiments showed that perfluorooctanoic acid and PFBA altered PPARα and PPARβ/δ protein expression, indicating potential PPAR-related responses in neuronal cells. These findings provide new human evidence for refining PFAS substitution strategies and advance our understanding of PFAS distribution in the CSF and potential neurotoxic implications.

articles.title:
MoodTOX:
A Multiscale Interpretable Graph Neural Network
for Out-of-Distribution Multiorgan Toxicity Prediction
articles.abstract: Abstract Expanding chemical production, application and environmental discharge raise multiorgan toxic risks originating from emerging contaminants and complicate precise toxicity prediction. Emerging computational toxicology models enable large-scale toxicity screening but suffer from distribution-shift-induced spurious correlations that impair out-of-distribution generalization and substructure toxicity attribution. Here, we present MoodTOX, a multiorgan molecular out-of-distribution toxicity prediction framework tailored to address this challenge. MoodTOX quantifies distributional heterogeneity across molecular structures and physicochemical properties and extracts stable toxicity-related features, thereby reducing model reliance on distribution-specific spurious correlations. It also reveals key structural contributions at chemical bond, atom and molecular-fragment levels to improve out-of-distribution generalization and interpretability. We validate MoodTOX by using public benchmark data sets alongside our self-curated multiorgan toxicity data set (>280,000 chemicals). It achieves mean AUC values ranging from 0.932 to 0.960 for respiratory toxicity, nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and hERG inhibition. On matched compounds retained within MoodTOX’s high-confidence applicability domain, MoodTOX achieved an average accuracy of 89.2% across four external validation data sets, corresponding to a 23.6% relative improvement over existing online prediction tools within these evaluated subsets. Through data curation, we further construct an external candidate library containing plastic additives, and establish a multiorgan toxicity screening strategy to identify potentially high-risk compounds. Ultimately, MoodTOX and its online prediction platform support high-accuracy early risk warning, priority screening and structural-mechanism interpretation of toxic hazards originating from emerging pollutants.

articles.title:
Biological Soil
Crusts Drive Microbial Community Assembly,
Mineral Weathering, and Soil Organic Matter Stabilization in Iron
Ore Tailings
articles.abstract: Abstract Mineral weathering and soil organic matter (OM) stabilization are critical to the eco-engineering of soil formation in iron (Fe) ore tailings for sustainable rehabilitation. Biological soil crusts (BSCs) are recognized as pioneer communities during early pedogenesis, yet their establishment in tailings and their roles in driving mineral weathering and OM stabilization remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the establishment of two BSCs, i.e., Leucobryum glaucum (LG) and Timmiella diminuta (TD), in Fe ore tailings and their functions in microbial community development, mineral weathering, and OM stabilization in a 56-day microcosm experiment. Both BSCs established visible crust cover and shaped microbial community composition toward heterotrophic and nitrogen-cycling taxa. BSC colonization lowered tailing pH from >8.8 to <8.5 and reduced electrical conductivity (EC) from >900 to <680 μS cm–1 under exogenous OM addition. Compared to uncolonized controls, BSC colonization improved OM accumulation in the form of particulate OM (POM), and LG colonization particularly enhanced OM stabilization through mineral-associated OM (MAOM) formation in tailings. This MAOM formation was underpinned by BSC-driven weathering of primary Fe-bearing phyllosilicates into secondary Fe/Al minerals, which heterogeneously trapped OM at the submicron scale, as revealed by nanoscale secondary ion mass spectrometry (NanoSIMS). Collectively, our findings demonstrate that BSCs drive coupled microbial community development, OM formation, and mineral-mediated stabilization during early tailings pedogenesis, providing mechanistic insights for harnessing BSCs in mine site rehabilitation.

articles.title:
Enhanced Droplet-Mode
Brown Carbon Formation at High
Relative Humidity in Urban Beijing: Size-Resolved Chromophore Evidence
for Aqueous Processing and Its Radiative Impacts
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric brown carbon (BrC) affects radiative forcing, yet how relative humidity (RH) modulates its size-dependent effects remains unclear. We conducted size-resolved measurements in urban Beijing during winter-early spring to investigate how RH modulates BrC size distributions, chromophore composition, and optical properties. Results show that the geometric mean diameter (GMD) of water-soluble BrC (WS-BrC) increased from ∼0.45 μm at low RH (≤40%) to ∼0.80 μm at high RH (≥60%), with less growth for water-insoluble BrC (WI-BrC). This growth was driven by an increased droplet-mode contribution (from ∼45% to ∼80%), and WS-BrC grew 1.6 times faster than WI-BrC. Chromophore analysis links this to aqueous processing: chromophores associated with aqueous formation pathways─nitrosalicylic acids, N-heterocyclics, and nitrocatechols─increased 13.2-, 9.8-, and 7.1-fold in droplet mode at high RH, versus 2.0–3.1-fold for primary emission chromophores. Mie calculations show that the RH-induced GMD shift moves WS-BrC into the steepest declining region of the single scattering albedo (SSA)–size curve, where size growth dominates the decrease of SSA and far outweighs the contribution of composition changes, implying stronger heating under humid conditions. These findings identify RH as a key modulator of BrC size distributions and optical properties via aqueous processing, highlighting the need for size- and RH-resolved BrC in climate models.

articles.title:
Shifts in Bacteria–DOM
Interactions Accompany
Changes in Methane Emissions with Weakening Glacial Influence in Proglacial
Lakes
articles.abstract: Abstract Proglacial lakes formed by glacial retreat are increasing in number and may feed back on climate change if they contribute to aquatic greenhouse gas emissions. However, this potential feedback depends on how microbial processing of dissolved organic matter (DOM) responds to climate change-related processes, such as weakening glacial influence, and on the potential consequences of these responses for methane (CH4) emissions. We investigated nine proglacial lakes on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau to characterize bacterial communities and DOM pools along a gradient of weakening glacial influence, and to assess how shifts in bacteria–DOM interactions are associated with CH4 emissions. We found that bacterial community assembly and DOM assembly were decoupled, with different responses to the same environmental pressures. With weakening glacial influence, the DOM pool in proglacial lakes may increasingly comprise relatively recalcitrant DOM components. Meanwhile, DOM production or transformation may become less dependent on specific bacteria–DOM interactions, while DOM degradation becomes increasingly specialized. Together, these shifts could favor the accumulation of substrates for methanogenesis and were associated with changes in methanogenic community composition and reduced potential resource competition between methanogens and bacteria, which may contribute to higher CH4 emissions from proglacial lakes. These findings reveal associations between weakening glacial influence and shifts in microbial carbon processing, providing new insights into potential climate feedbacks from expanding proglacial lakes.

articles.title:
How to Be More Effective
in Supporting Evidence-Informed
Decision-Making for Sustainable Development
articles.abstract: Abstract It is widely accepted that the 2030 target for achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) will not be met, largely because of the failure to translate scientific knowledge into policy, governance, and action at scale. Strengthening science-policy interfaces (SPIs) has been identified as a key measure for the mobilization of science for sustainable development. Effective SPIs rely on scientists and engineers to provide scientific knowledge as an input for evidence-based decision-making. Whether scientists and engineers act individually or collectively, their SPI engagement reflects the incentives and support of the system in which they are embedded (i.e., for academic scientists, the institutions of higher education and research, and funding agencies). Thus, systemic changes are needed to increase the extent and effectiveness of individual and collective SPI engagement and to make science-policy interfaces more transformative. Within the research and education sector, such changes would include reforming research assessment to incentivize SPI engagement; targeted training in SPI skills; and providing incentives, training, and support to promote knowledge coproduction. Additional changes, such as strengthening knowledge brokering capacities and SPI advisory mechanisms and aligning SPIs with transformative change goals, would extend beyond the research and education sector, necessitating coproductive engagement with actors in the policy sector.

articles.title:
Artificial
Intelligence for Methane Detection: From
Continuous Monitoring to Verified Mitigation
articles.abstract: Abstract Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, responsible for roughly 30% of warming since preindustrial times. A small number of large point sources account for a disproportionate share of emissions, creating an opportunity for substantial reductions by targeting relatively few sites. Detection and attribution of large emissions at scale for notifying asset owners remains challenging. Here, we introduce MARS-S2L, a machine learning model that detects methane emissions in publicly available multispectral satellite imagery. Trained on a manually curated data set of over 80,000 images, the model provides high-resolution detections every 2 days, enabling facility-level attribution and identifying 78% of plumes with an 8% false-positive rate at 697 previously unseen sites. Deployed operationally, MARS-S2L has issued 2,776 notifications to stakeholders in 25 countries, enabling verified, permanent mitigation of six persistent emitters, including a superemitter in Algeria that had been releasing approximately 27,500 tonnes of methane annually for at least a decade and a previously unknown emitter in Libya first identified by MARS-S2L. These results demonstrate a scalable pathway from satellite detection to quantifiable methane mitigation.

articles.title:
Mechanistic
Interpretation
of Machine Learning Model
Explanations Depends on Data and Model Design: Evidence from Activated
Carbon Filtration
articles.abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms governing complex environmental systems is a central challenge across environmental science and engineering. Where mechanistic understanding is incomplete, machine learning (ML) combined with explainable AI methods─particularly Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)─has been increasingly applied to environmental data sets, with the resulting explanations often interpreted as reflections of underlying process mechanisms. However, the extent to which SHAP explanations reflect true system behavior depends on the conditions under which the model was developed. Here, we systematically investigate how model class, data regime, and hyperparameter configuration as components of the learning environment affect the mechanistic consistency of SHAP-based explanations, using granular activated carbon (GAC) filtration for micropollutant removal from wastewater as a case study. We show that all three components impact explanations and their consistency with proven mechanisms. Model class can affect which feature interactions are captured; the characteristics of the training data─both distribution and lacking coverage of joint feature space regions─shape which relationships can be learned; and hyperparameter sensitivity differs substantially between model classes. These findings demonstrate that SHAP explanations cannot be interpreted independently of the learning environment, but we argue that they can still serve as a valuable tool for hypothesis generation in environmental ML applications.

articles.title:
Using Street View
and Remote Sensing Imagery to Estimate
NO2 and PM2.5 Concentrations for the Continental
US
articles.abstract: Abstract Land use regression (LUR) models are widely used for estimating fine-scale ambient air quality. Street view and remote sensing imagery are emerging sources to measure built environment features which may enhance traditional LUR predictors and further improve model performance. In this study, we investigate using various combinations of street view and remote sensing derived features to develop national annual NO2 and PM2.5 machine learning models (2007–2020). Predictors in our models include: (1) Google Street View (GSV) imagery derived semantic features, (2) satellite-based aerosol estimates, and (3) Landsat-derived spectral indices and elevation. Full models combining all predictors achieved the best model performance, with random 10-fold cross validation R2 values of 0.92 for NO2 and 0.75 for PM2.5. Models incorporating GSV-derived features generally achieve enhanced model fit. Beyond conventional internal model evaluation, we examined how different predictors impact the spatial patterns of model prediction surfaces. GSV-informed models yielded a wider range of model estimates and better captured intraurban air pollution variability─a finding confirmed by external validation using independent mobile monitoring and calibrated PurpleAir measurements. Our results highlight the potential of street-view imagery to characterize fine-scale spatial gradients in air pollution and thus support more spatially resolved exposure assessment.

articles.title: Mechanisms and Prediction of Microcystis Removal by Sediment Resuspension in Drinking-Water Reservoirs
articles.abstract: Abstract Microcystis blooms threaten drinking-water quality, yet sustainable in situ controls are needed. A survey of 43 drinking-water reservoirs in eastern China and the Tibetan Plateau found moderate- to high-intensity blooms in 26% of the reservoirs. We evaluated sediment resuspension (SR) as a nature-based intervention. Experiments with ten sediments showed that Microcystis removal (35.0% ± 14.3%) coincided with declining dissolved Fe and Al. Experiments and scanning electron microscopy–energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM–EDS) identified Fe/Al-mediated flocculation and settling, rather than particles alone, as the primary short-term removal pathway. Sediment composition regulated reactive Fe/Al supply and utilization: maximum Fe+Al removal increased with active Fe+Al content (R2 = 0.88, p < 0.001), whereas flocculation effectiveness declined as the fine-particle fraction (<63 μm) increased (R2 = 0.67, p < 0.03). We developed a sediment-property-based model from these relationships. Across more than 30 reservoirs in eastern China, predicted Microcystis removal averaged (1.37 ± 1.97) × 108 cells L–1. In a Microcystis-dominated reservoir, predicted and field-fitted removal rates differed by 6%. Observations from five filamentous-cyanobacteria-dominated reservoirs suggested Fe/Al-related flocculation may also aid removal of other taxa. This study provides a mechanistic, predictive basis for evaluating SR in bloom management.

articles.title:
Laboratory and Field
Investigation of Amines in Automotive
Brake Wear Particles
articles.abstract: Abstract Nonexhaust vehicle emissions (brake wear, tire wear, and road dust) now dominate particulate matter (PM) sources in urban environments as tailpipe emissions continue to decline. Among these, brake wear particles (BWPs) remain under-characterized, particularly their organic composition. This study investigates the formation and atmospheric relevance of amines released during the thermal degradation of phenolic resin, the primary binder in brake pads. Controlled brake dynamometer and phenolic-resin thermal degradation experiments were performed together with field measurements adjacent to two Southern California freeways (I-5, Santa Ana, and I-710, Long Beach). High-resolution mass spectrometry analysis revealed the prevalence of nitrogen-containing compounds across all data sets with dicyclohexylamine (C12H23N; DCHA) consistently detected in laboratory and ambient particles. DCHA concentrations in laboratory particles ranged from 0.08 to 1.6 ng/μg across brake pad types and resin conditions. DCHA was measured in air sampled onto filters at levels ranging from 2.1 ± 1.6 pg m–3 (Santa Ana) to 3.5 ± 1.7 pg m–3 (Long Beach). Ambient levels of DCHA correlated with near-road NO and brake-associated metals (Fe, Ba), suggesting a possible link between its emission and braking activity. These findings identify brake wear as a previously under-recognized source of DCHA and related organic nitrogen compounds, often associated primarily with tire wear emissions.

articles.title:
Biomass-Derived
Supramolecular Living Hydrogels for
Adaptive Dye Wastewater Remediation
articles.abstract: Abstract Dye wastewater from textile, leather, and paper industries poses a persistent threat to aquatic ecosystems owing to its chemical recalcitrance and potential toxicity. Microalgae provide a sustainable strategy for dye bioremediation through synergistic bioaccumulation and biodegradation. However, these microbes suffer from limited tolerance to the complex composition of dye wastewater and are difficult to recycle after treatment. Here, we report retrievable living microalgae-loaded polysaccharide hydrogel networks coated with tannic acid (MPH@TA) for efficient purification of wastewater containing diverse dyes. The flexible supramolecular networks containing Chlorella pyrenoidosa create a protective microenvironment that supports robust microalgal growth and efficient dye removal while reducing the leakage of microalgae. Notably, MPH@TA achieves removal efficiencies of 97.7% and 94.5% for 100 mg L–1 malachite green and reactive red, respectively, highlighting its implementation for both cationic and anionic dyes. The living MPH@TA system enables facile recyclability and effective treatment of complex real dye wastewater. Transcriptomic analysis shows that MPH@TA modulates the antioxidant defense, redox metabolism, and respiratory energy supply of microalgae, thereby enhancing microalgal tolerance and biotransformation of dye molecules. This work not only provides a simple yet efficient strategy for water purification but also advances insights into microbe–material hybrid interactions for engineered living materials.

articles.title:
Revisiting
the Climate
Benefits Provided by Wood through
Future-Oriented Material and Energy Displacement
articles.abstract: Abstract Displacement factors (DFs) quantify climate benefits of wood-based products relative to non-wood alternatives. Existing DFs are typically static whereas economy-wide decarbonization motivates a forward-looking assessment. Previous work focuses on semifinished materials and lacks harmonized, transparent modeling. This study provides an open-access, unit-process-based database of future-oriented DFs for 81 wood-product-material-variants across six end-use categories. It uses time-explicit life cycle assessment (LCA), which links processes to the technology landscape as they occur, under three decarbonization scenarios for 2020–2070. Wood-based products showed positive DFs in 2020, with weighted averages from near-zero for furniture to 1.04 kg C/kg C for chemicals and textiles, though lower than previous estimates. DFs declined over time for all products except chemicals, most steeply under climate-ambitious scenarios. Wood sustained the highest benefit in the least ambitious scenario. The decline was driven by faster decarbonization of non-wood products that contain proportionally more fossil-intensive components. Time-explicit LCA yielded lower DFs for long-lived products as end-of-life processes were assigned to more decarbonized future years, an effect not captured by conventional or prospective LCA. Energy-related DFs approached near-zero by 2070. The findings support redirecting wood flows from energy toward long-lived material applications and caution against harvest intensification justified on displacement arguments alone.

articles.title:
Complementary Mechanisms
for Fe(II)-Mediated Nickel
and Cobalt Release from Laterites
articles.abstract: Abstract Nickel (Ni) and cobalt (Co) mining must increase as renewable energy generation and energy storage technologies expand. Most of the world’s Ni is found in laterite deposits, but the processing of these ores is costly, energy-intensive, and damaging to the environment. Here, we present a novel ferrous leaching approach that operates at ambient conditions (22 °C, pH 7.5) to recover Ni and Co from four lateritic domains from the Barnes Hill Deposit in Tasmania, Australia. Ni and Co K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) shows that most of the Ni is bound in iron (Fe) (oxyhydr)oxide and silicate phases, whereas Co is predominantly associated with manganese (Mn) oxide minerals. Under optimal leach conditions, up to 38% of Ni and approximately 100% of Co are recovered. XAS analysis on the leached samples shows that Co (and Mn) release occurs by Fe(II)-induced reductive dissolution of Mn oxides. In the case of Ni, 57Fe-isotope tracer results suggest Fe(II)-catalyzed mineral recrystallization is repartitioning solid-phase Ni to a more labile form, while Ni hosted in silicate phases such as serpentine can also be extracted with a mild acid wash. Our results demonstrate that ferrous leaching is highly effective at solubilizing Co (and Ni) and thus may be a viable strategy for processing Co-rich laterites as well as metal-bearing Mn oxides such as deep-sea nodules and crusts.

articles.title:
When Selectivity
Is Not Enough: Product-Centered Metrics
for Environmental Separations
articles.abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration (NF) has traditionally been evaluated through the lens of water production, utilizing water/solute selectivity as the primary performance metric. As NF increasingly targets selective solute fractionation for resource recovery, the focus has shifted toward solute/solute selectivity. However, relying solely on selectivity can be fundamentally misleading because it frequently misaligns with practical process objectives. Furthermore, evaluating materials strictly based on instantaneous selectivity can potentially obscure the true process-level viability. This Perspective redefines performance evaluation by establishing a unified, product-centered framework applicable across three distinct separation scenarios: recovering the permeate, the retentate, or both streams as valuable products. To this end, we introduce a new framework based on the recovery-retention diagram to evaluate generic binary separations. This framework demonstrates how separation outcomes are intrinsically governed by both membrane performance and feed composition, which can be captured by the separation trajectory. Ultimately, transitioning from a purely selectivity-based evaluation framework to a product-centered one bridges the critical gap between bench-scale material discovery and scalable process engineering.
